Subject: Important recall: Corvane children’s ibuprofen dosing syringe

We know many parents are worried about the Corvane children’s ibuprofen recall. We’re sorry for the worry this has caused, and we want to explain what is affected and what to do.

Corvane Pharma has voluntarily recalled the dosing syringe supplied with:

Pediatric Ibuprofen Oral Suspension 100 mg/5 mL, berry flavour, 120 mL bottle
Lots CV6114A and CV6114B
Expiry 08/2027

If you have a Corvane bottle at home, check the lot number on the bottom of the box first. Lot CV6114B is one of the affected lots.

The problem is the printing on the syringe, not the medicine. Corvane says the suspension meets its specifications and is not contaminated. The syringe markings show half the actual volume: the line labelled 2.5 mL holds 5 mL, and the line labelled 5 mL holds 10 mL. Using the supplied syringe according to its markings could give a child approximately twice the intended dose.

If you have one of the affected lots, discard the syringe that came in the box. Use a correctly marked oral syringe instead. You can also return the product for a full refund.

Free replacement syringes are expected at Cedarbrook before noon today, Monday, November 9. They’re available to anyone who needs one; no receipt is required. We’ll also be open Saturday from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. for exchanges.

If you have any doubt about a dose already given, call the Ontario Poison Centre at 1-800-268-9017. They can assess your child’s situation. The advice depends on things like the child’s weight, how much and how often medicine was given, and their health. Don’t give another dose until the poison centre or a doctor says it’s okay.

Call 911 or go to the emergency department if your child is very sleepy or hard to wake, is vomiting blood, is not peeing, or has a seizure.

We received notice of the recall on the evening of November 6 and put signs on our door and by the children’s aisle the next morning. Many of these bottles were sold over the counter without a patient profile or phone number, so we could not contact every purchaser directly. Please share this notice with anyone who may have an affected bottle.
